1: # MCP acceptance harness (Phase 0)
2: 
3: A standalone, black-box acceptance harness for the production CommonCal MCP
4: endpoint. It targets a configurable production-component URL and asserts:
5: 
6: - **Phase 0.1** — the JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake is standards-compatible
7:   (MCP Streamable HTTP);
8: - **Phase 0.2** — the public OAuth challenge and discovery contract hold;
9: - **Phase 0.3** — DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the
10:   authenticated MCP lifecycle (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
11:   `tools/list`, `tools/call calendar_list`) complete;
12: - **Phase 0.4** — wrong issuer/audience/signature/expiry/client tokens, missing
13:   grant, revoked grant, and broadened grant fail closed, and two concurrent
14:   authenticated clients cannot observe each other's identity.
15: 
16: This harness is **not** the slice1-lab. It does not launch the lab binaries and
17: does not treat the lab binary as a release artifact. It reuses the lab's
18: fixture shapes (the `initialize` request shape from
19: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` case 10, the DCR request shape from
20: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` `fresh_dcr`, the standard access-token claim
21: contract from `slice1-lab/src/jwt.rs`, the scope catalog from
22: `slice1-lab/src/common.rs`, and the negative-token / fail-closed cases from
23: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` cases 3-9 and `slice1-lab/PROOF.md` P7), and the
24: MCP/OAuth standards-compliance expectations. It owns its own production-facing
25: configuration, lifecycle, reporting, and cleanup: it is a pure HTTP client,
26: starts no servers, and leaves no processes behind.
27: 
28: ## Baseline expectation (Phase 0.1)
29: 
30: Against the **current** production component, `initialize` is **not**
31: standards-compatible. The custom gateway dispatcher (`mcp-server/src/gateway.rs`)
32: only recognizes `tools/list` and `tools/call`, so `initialize` returns HTTP 400
33: with JSON-RPC error `-32601 Method not found`.
34: 
35: The harness asserts standards-compliance and therefore **exits non-zero**
36: against the current production component. That failure is the **intentional,
37: asserted exit condition** for this phase: it documents the current broken state
38: that later phases (Phase 2, `mcp-rmcp-gateway`) must fix. The harness is the
39: regression gate: it stays red until the production component implements a
40: standards-compatible `initialize`.
41: 
42: ## Phase 0.2: public challenge and OAuth discovery
43: 
44: `discovery.js` asserts the public OAuth discovery contract against the same
45: configurable production-component URL:
46: 
47: - **A1** — an unauthenticated JSON-RPC `initialize` request receives HTTP 401
48:   (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error (e.g. HTTP 400 with
49:   JSON-RPC `-32601`);
50: - **A2** — the 401 challenge carries a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` header whose
51:   `resource_metadata` parameter is the configured public protected-resource
52:   metadata URL (the MCP endpoint origin plus
53:   `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and never a loopback or lab URL
54:   (e.g. the hard-coded `http://127.0.0.1:3001` in
55:   `mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541`);
56: - **A3** — the protected-resource metadata document parses as JSON and names
57:   the configured authorization-server issuer in `authorization_servers`;
58: - **A4** — the authorization-server metadata document (RFC 8414 location, with
59:   the OIDC discovery location as fallback) parses as JSON and supplies usable
60:   `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `registration_endpoint`, and
61:   `jwks_uri` values (absolute http(s) URLs; https when the issuer is public).
62: 
63: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.2): against the **current** production component,
64: A1, A2, and A4 **fail** and A3 passes. Verified current state (2026-09-17,
65: `docs/MCP-PRODUCTION-FIX-PLAN.md`): `initialize` returns HTTP 400 with
66: `-32601` (no challenge is ever issued for the initial request); the 401
67: builders that do exist hard-code the lab loopback URL;
68: `https://mcal.hajnal.space/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is valid JSON
69: advertising `https://cal.hajnal.space`; and

A standalone, black-box acceptance harness for the production CommonCal MCP

  (MCP Streamable HTTP);
- **Phase 0.2** — the public OAuth challenge and discovery contract hold;
- **Phase 0.3** — DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the
  authenticated MCP lifecycle (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
  `tools/list`, `tools/call calendar_list`) complete;
- **Phase 0.4** — wrong issuer/audience/signature/expiry/client tokens, missing
  grant, revoked grant, and broadened grant fail closed, and two concurrent
  authenticated clients cannot observe each other's identity.

This harness is **not** the slice1-lab. It does not launch the lab binaries and
does not treat the lab binary as a release artifact. It reuses the lab's
fixture shapes (the `initialize` request shape from
`slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` case 10, the DCR request shape from
`slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` `fresh_dcr`, the standard access-token claim
contract from `slice1-lab/src/jwt.rs`, the scope catalog from
`slice1-lab/src/common.rs`, and the negative-token / fail-closed cases from
`slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` cases 3-9 and `slice1-lab/PROOF.md` P7), and the
MCP/OAuth standards-compliance expectations. It owns its own production-facing
configuration, lifecycle, reporting, and cleanup: it is a pure HTTP client,
starts no servers, and leaves no processes behind.

## Baseline expectation (Phase 0.1)

Against the **current** production component, `initialize` is **not**
standards-compatible. The custom gateway dispatcher (`mcp-server/src/gateway.rs`)
only recognizes `tools/list` and `tools/call`, so `initialize` returns HTTP 400
with JSON-RPC error `-32601 Method not found`.

The harness asserts standards-compliance and therefore **exits non-zero**
against the current production component. That failure is the **intentional,
asserted exit condition** for this phase: it documents the current broken state
that later phases (Phase 2, `mcp-rmcp-gateway`) must fix. The harness is the
regression gate: it stays red until the production component implements a
standards-compatible `initialize`.

## Phase 0.2: public challenge and OAuth discovery

`discovery.js` asserts the public OAuth discovery contract against the same
configurable production-component URL:

- **A1** — an unauthenticated JSON-RPC `initialize` request receives HTTP 401
  (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error (e.g. HTTP 400 with
  JSON-RPC `-32601`);
- **A2** — the 401 challenge carries a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` header whose
  `resource_metadata` parameter is the configured public protected-resource
  metadata URL (the MCP endpoint origin plus
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and never a loopback or lab URL
  (e.g. the hard-coded `http://127.0.0.1:3001` in
  `mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541`);
- **A3** — the protected-resource metadata document parses as JSON and names
  the configured authorization-server issuer in `authorization_servers`;
- **A4** — the authorization-server metadata document (RFC 8414 location, with
  the OIDC discovery location as fallback) parses as JSON and supplies usable
  `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `registration_endpoint`, and
  `jwks_uri` values (absolute http(s) URLs; https when the issuer is public).

Baseline expectation (Phase 0.2): against the **current** production component,
A1, A2, and A4 **fail** and A3 passes. Verified current state (2026-09-17,
`docs/MCP-PRODUCTION-FIX-PLAN.md`): `initialize` returns HTTP 400 with
`-32601` (no challenge is ever issued for the initial request); the 401
builders that do exist hard-code the lab loopback URL;
`https://mcal.hajnal.space/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is valid JSON
advertising `https://cal.hajnal.space`; and
`https://cal.hajnal.space/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the
CommonCal SPA HTML, not authorization-server metadata. The harness therefore
**exits non-zero** against the current production component — the intentional,
asserted exit condition for this phase and the regression gate for later
phases.

```sh
node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
# or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
  node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
```

| Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
| `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
| `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |

Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
intentional Phase 0.2 baseline against the current production component);
`2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
`$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-discovery.json`.

`oauth-lifecycle.js` asserts the full OAuth + MCP lifecycle against the same
configurable production-component URL:

- **L1** — DCR (RFC 7591) registration succeeds with the supported OpenCode
  loopback redirect shape (201, `client_id` present, no `client_secret`);
- **L2** — Authorization Code flow with `state` and S256 PKCE completes (code
  present, state round-trips);
- **L3** — token exchange completes and yields a resource-bound access token
  (3-part JWT) without manual JWT construction;
- **L4** — with that token, `initialize` succeeds (200, `protocolVersion`,
  `capabilities`, `serverInfo`);
- **L5** — `notifications/initialized` is accepted (202);
- **L6** — `tools/list` returns the expected nine tools, each with a

```sh

MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \

| `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |

- **S5** — wrong-client token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S6** — missing grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;

| -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
| `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |

```

### Configuration (environment variables)

| Variable               | Default                          | Description                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`              | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.               |
| `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `2025-03-26`                     | The `protocolVersion` to negotiate.          |
| `MCP_CLIENT_NAME`      | `commoncal-mcp-acceptance`       | `clientInfo.name` in the initialize request. |
| `MCP_CLIENT_VERSION`   | `0.1.0`                          | `clientInfo.version` in the initialize req.  |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`       | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.             |
| `MCP_RECORD_DIR`       | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic response record is written. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                        |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | `initialize` is standards-compatible (PASS).                   |
| `1`  | `initialize` is NOT standards-compatible (FAIL) — the intentional Phase 0.1 baseline exit condition against the current production component. |
| `2`  | Harness error (invalid configuration, network failure, unexpected error). |

### Deterministic record

The harness writes a deterministic record of the request and response (object
keys sorted, volatile headers dropped) to
`$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-initialize.json` (default: the OS temp
directory). The path is printed on every run.

## CI usage

In CI, point the harness at a production-equivalent deployment and treat a
non-zero exit as a real failure once the production component is fixed. During
Phase 0 the harness is expected to be red; record the failure as the baseline.

```sh
# Example CI step (production-equivalent deployment)
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
  MCP_RECORD_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/mcp-acceptance" \
  node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
```

## Verification (harness self-test)

A verification-only mock server exercises both the PASS and FAIL paths without
touching production. It is not a release artifact.

```sh
# Start the mock server in one terminal
node mcp-acceptance/mock/server.js

# In another terminal:
# FAIL path — mock mirrors the CURRENT production behavior (expect exit 1)
MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-current node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
echo "exit: $?"   # -> 1

# PASS path — mock returns a standards-compatible initialize (expect exit 0)
MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-compliant node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
echo "exit: $?"   # -> 0
```

Self-contained verifiers (they start and clean up the mock server themselves):

```sh
# Phase 0.1 harness: both exit paths (default mock port 3999)
node mcp-acceptance/verify.js

# Phase 0.2 discovery harness: both exit paths with focused A1/A2/A4
# violations on the FAIL path and a passing A3 (default mock port 3998,
# issuer host 3999; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-discovery.js

# Phase 0.3 oauth-lifecycle harness: both exit paths (default mock port 4001,
# issuer host 4002; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-oauth-lifecycle.js

# Phase 0.4 security-isolation harness: both exit paths (default mock port
# 4003, issuer host 4004; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-security-isolation.js
```

The Phase 0.1/0.2 mock (`mock/server.js`) mirrors production's two-host
topology: the MCP host (MOCK_PORT) serves the MCP endpoint and the
protected-resource metadata; the issuer host (MOCK_ISSUER_PORT, default
MOCK_PORT + 1) serves the authorization-server metadata (SPA HTML in the
current mode, valid JSON in the compliant mode).

The Phase 0.3/0.4 mock (`mock/lifecycle-server.js`) is driven by a single
world selector (`MOCK_WORLD`, default `compliant`; `current` mirrors
production today). In the compliant world it implements the full OAuth + MCP
lifecycle (DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, JWKS, and the
authenticated MCP lifecycle) plus verification-only test hooks (`/_test/*`)
for driving the negative token and grant-state cases. In the current world it
mirrors the verified current production state (the authorization service is
not deployed; the MCP gateway does not implement the MCP lifecycle).

## Files

- `harness.js` — the Phase 0.1 standalone black-box harness (initialize
  standards-compliance).
- `discovery.js` — the Phase 0.2 standalone black-box harness (public 401
  challenge + protected-resource and authorization-server metadata discovery).
- `oauth-lifecycle.js` — the Phase 0.3 standalone black-box harness (DCR,
  Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the authenticated MCP
  lifecycle through `calendar_list`).
- `security-isolation.js` — the Phase 0.4 standalone black-box harness
  (fail-closed token/grant cases and concurrent-identity isolation).
- `lib.js` — shared helpers for the Phase 0.3/0.4 harnesses (OAuth flow, MCP
  calls, JWT helpers, deterministic JSON).
- `fixtures/initialize-request.json` — the `initialize` request fixture (reused
  from the slice1-lab request shape; owned by this harness).
- `verify.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.1 harness exit
  paths.
- `verify-discovery.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.2
  harness exit paths, including the focused A1/A2/A4 violations and the
  passing A3 on the FAIL path.
- `verify-oauth-lifecycle.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.3
  harness exit paths.
- `verify-security-isolation.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase
  0.4 harness exit paths.
- `mock/server.js` — verification-only mock server for Phase 0.1/0.2 (PASS +
  FAIL fixtures, two-host topology).
- `mock/lifecycle-server.js` — verification-only mock server for Phase 0.3/0.4
  (full OAuth + MCP lifecycle, world selector, test hooks).
- `mock/oauth-provider.js` — verification-only mock OAuth provider (DCR,
  Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, JWKS, token validation,
  grants, token minting).
- `README.md` — this document.

586:         match grants.len() {
587:             0 => Ok(None),
588:             1 => Ok(Some(grants.into_iter().next().unwrap())),
589:             _ => Err(InternalError::Http(
590:                 500,
591:                 "ambiguous grant response: expected at most one grant".to_string(),
592:             )),
593:         }
594:     }
595: 
596:     pub async fn check_idempotency(
597:         &self,
598:         operation_id: &str,
599:     ) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, InternalError> {
600:         let url = self
601:             .api_base
602:             .join(&format!("internal/mcp/idempotency/{}", operation_id))
603:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
604:         let resp = self
605:             .http_client
606:             .get(url.as_str())
607:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
608:             .send()
609:             .await
610:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
611: 
612:         if resp.status() == 404 {
613:             return Ok(None);
614:         }
615: 
616:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
617:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
618:                 resp.status().as_u16(),
619:                 "check_idempotency failed".to_string(),
620:             ));
621:         }
622: 
623:         let body: serde_json::Value = resp
624:             .json()
625:             .await
626:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Deserialize(e.to_string()))?;
627: 
628:         Ok(Some(body))
629:     }

631:     pub async fn record_idempotency(
632:         &self,
633:         operation_id: &str,
634:         payload: &serde_json::Value,
635:     ) -> Result<(), InternalError> {
636:         let url = self
637:             .api_base
638:             .join("internal/mcp/idempotency")
639:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
640:         let resp = self
641:             .http_client
642:             .post(url.as_str())
643:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
644:             .json(&serde_json::json!({
645:                 "operation_id": operation_id,
646:                 "payload": payload,
647:             }))
648:             .send()
649:             .await
650:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
651: 
652:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
653:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
654:                 resp.status().as_u16(),
655:                 "record_idempotency failed".to_string(),
656:             ));
657:         }
658: 
659:         Ok(())
660:     }
661: }

663: #[derive(Debug)]
664: pub enum InternalError {
665:     Connection(String),
666:     Http(u16, String),
667:     Deserialize(String),
668: }

670: impl std::fmt::Display for InternalError {
671:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
672:         match self {
673:             Self::Connection(msg) => write!(f, "connection error: {}", msg),
674:             Self::Http(code, msg) => write!(f, "http {}: {}", code, msg),
675:             Self::Deserialize(msg) => write!(f, "deserialize error: {}", msg),
676:         }
677:     }
678: }

2: //!
3: //! All values are loopback test values. Nothing here is a real secret or a
4: //! production URL. The scope catalog mirrors the CommonCal scope catalog that
5: //! the real consent adapter (Slice 2) will enforce.

9: /// The fixed CommonCal scope catalog. Consent may only grant scopes in this set.
10: pub const SCOPE_CATALOG: &[&str] = &[
11:     "commoncal.calendar.metadata.read",
12:     "commoncal.availability.read",
13:     "commoncal.event.read.basic",
14:     "commoncal.event.read.details",
15:     "commoncal.event.create",

17:     "commoncal.event.delete",
18:     "commoncal.reminder.read",

20: ];
21: 
22: /// A scope deliberately outside the catalog, used to prove consent fails closed.
23: pub const EVIL_SCOPE: &str = "evil.unknown.scope";
24: 
25: /// The fixed test subject (numeric, matches the future CommonCal user ID contract).
26: pub const FIXED_SUBJECT: &str = "1";
27: 
28: /// The exact MCP resource / audience the consent adapter is allowed to grant.
29: pub const RESOURCE_URL: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp";
30: 
31: /// Candidate authorization service issuer (loopback only).
32: pub const AUTH_ISSUER: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:4000";
33: 
34: /// The MCP echo endpoint base URL (loopback).
35: pub const MCP_ECHO: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:3001";
36: 
37: /// The exact loopback redirect URI registered for the DCR client.
38: pub const LOOPBACK_REDIRECT: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:8321/callback";
39: 
40: /// The fixed test approval: the scopes the one fixed test subject approves.
41: /// For the lab this is the full catalog. In production this is the user's choice.
42: pub fn fixed_approval() -> Vec<String> {
43:     SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
44: }
45: 
46: /// Compute `requested ∩ catalog ∩ fixed-approval`. This is the ONLY set of
47: /// scopes the consent adapter may grant. Unknown scopes are dropped.
48: pub fn granted_scopes(requested: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
49:     let approval_vec = fixed_approval();
50:     let approval: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
51:         approval_vec.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
52:     let catalog: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().copied().collect();
53:     let mut out = Vec::new();
54:     for scope in requested {
55:         let s: &str = scope.as_str();
56:         if catalog.contains(s) && approval.contains(s) {
57:             out.push(scope.clone());
58:         }
59:     }
60:     out.sort();
61:     out.dedup();
62:     out
63: }
64:

73: }

89: }

54: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
55: struct CurrentClaims {
56:     user_id: i64,
57:     client_id: String,
58:     _scopes: Vec<String>,
59: }
60: 
61: static CURRENT_CLAIMS: LazyLock<RwLock<Option<CurrentClaims>>> =
62:     LazyLock::new(|| RwLock::new(None));

64: /// The CommonCal internal API base URL (loopback).
65: fn commoncal_base() -> String {
66:     std::env::var("MCP_ECHO_COMMONCAL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "http://127.0.0.1:4002".to_string())
67: }
68: 
69: /// The bridge key for the CommonCal internal API (lab value).
70: fn commoncal_bridge_key() -> String {
71:     std::env::var("MCP_ECHO_BRIDGE_KEY")
72:         .unwrap_or_else(|_| "slice1-loopback-bridge-key".to_string())
73: }
74: 
75: /// Build an rmcp ErrorData with an internal error code.
76: fn err(message: impl Into<String>) -> rmcp::ErrorData {
77:     rmcp::ErrorData::new(rmcp::model::ErrorCode::INTERNAL_ERROR, message.into(), None)
78: }

80: /// Shared HTTP client for the CommonCal internal API (lab-only, loopback).
81: static ECHO_HTTP: LazyLock<reqwest::Client> = LazyLock::new(|| {
82:     reqwest::Client::builder()
83:         .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))
84:         .build()
85:         .expect("http client")
86: });

101:     #[tool(description = "List the calendars available to the authenticated user.")]
102:     async fn calendar_list(&self) -> Result<CallToolResult, rmcp::ErrorData> {
103:         // Read the authenticated claims set by the axum middleware.
104:         let claims = CURRENT_CLAIMS
105:             .read()
106:             .await
107:             .clone()
108:             .ok_or_else(|| err("unauthenticated"))?;
109: 
110:         let base = commoncal_base();
111:         let key = commoncal_bridge_key();
112: 
113:         // 1. Check the active mcp_grant for (user_id, client_id).
114:         let grant_url = format!(
115:             "{}/internal/grant?user_id={}&client_id={}",
116:             base,
117:             claims.user_id,
118:             urlencoding::encode(&claims.client_id)
119:         );
120:         let grant_resp = ECHO_HTTP
121:             .get(&grant_url)
122:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", key))
123:             .send()
124:             .await
125:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("grant lookup transport: {e}")))?;
126:         let grant_status = grant_resp.status();
127:         if grant_status.as_u16() == 404 {
128:             return Err(err("no active MCP grant — consent required"));
129:         }
130:         if !grant_status.is_success() {
131:             return Err(err(format!("grant lookup failed: {grant_status}")));
132:         }
133:         let grant_body: serde_json::Value = grant_resp
134:             .json()
135:             .await
136:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("grant parse: {e}")))?;
137:         let allowed_ids: Vec<i64> = grant_body
138:             .pointer("/grant/allowed_calendar_ids")
139:             .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
140:             .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_i64()).collect())
141:             .unwrap_or_default();
142: 
143:         // 2. Fetch the user's real calendars from the CommonCal internal API.
144:         let cal_url = format!("{}/internal/calendars/{}", base, claims.user_id);
145:         let cal_resp = ECHO_HTTP
146:             .get(&cal_url)
147:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", key))
148:             .send()
149:             .await
150:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("calendar fetch transport: {e}")))?;
151:         if !cal_resp.status().is_success() {
152:             return Err(err(format!("calendar fetch failed: {}", cal_resp.status())));
153:         }
154:         let cal_body: serde_json::Value = cal_resp
155:             .json()
156:             .await
157:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("calendar parse: {e}")))?;
158:         let calendars: Vec<serde_json::Value> = cal_body
159:             .get("calendars")
160:             .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
161:             .cloned()
162:             .unwrap_or_default();
163: 
164:         // 3. Filter by the grant's allowed calendar IDs.
165:         let filtered: Vec<serde_json::Value> = calendars
166:             .into_iter()
167:             .filter(|c| {
168:                 c.get("id")
169:                     .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())
170:                     .is_some_and(|id| allowed_ids.contains(&id))
171:             })
172:             .collect();
173: 
174:         let output = json!({ "calendars": filtered });
175:         Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(
176:             serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output).unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
177:         )]))
178:     }

182:     #[tool(
183:         description = "Find availability slots for the specified calendars within a time range."
184:     )]
185:     async fn availability_find(
186:         &self,
187:         params: Parameters<AvailabilityFindParams>,
188:     ) -> Result<CallToolResult, rmcp::ErrorData> {
189:         let claims = CURRENT_CLAIMS
190:             .read()
191:             .await
192:             .clone()
193:             .ok_or_else(|| err("unauthenticated"))?;
194: 
195:         let (allowed_ids, scopes) = load_grant(&claims).await?;
196:         require_scope(&scopes, "commoncal.availability.read")?;
197:         validate_range(&params.0.from, &params.0.to)?;
198: 
199:         let base = commoncal_base();
200:         let key = commoncal_bridge_key();
201:         let mut all_slots = Vec::new();
202: 
203:         for cal_id in &params.0.calendar_ids {
204:             require_calendar(&allowed_ids, *cal_id)?;
205:             let url = format!(
206:                 "{}/internal/availability?calendar_id={}&from={}&to={}",
207:                 base,
208:                 cal_id,
209:                 urlencoding::encode(&params.0.from),
210:                 urlencoding::encode(&params.0.to)
211:             );
212:             let resp = ECHO_HTTP
213:                 .get(&url)
214:                 .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", key))
215:                 .send()
216:                 .await
217:                 .map_err(|e| err(format!("availability transport: {e}")))?;
218:             if !resp.status().is_success() {
219:                 return Err(err(format!("availability failed: {}", resp.status())));
220:             }
221:             let body: serde_json::Value = resp
222:                 .json()
223:                 .await
224:                 .map_err(|e| err(format!("availability parse: {e}")))?;
225:             if let Some(slots) = body.get("slots").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
226:                 all_slots.extend(slots.iter().cloned());
227:             }
228:         }
229: 
230:         let output = json!({ "slots": all_slots });
231:         Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(
232:             serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output).unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
233:         )]))
234:     }

236:     #[tool(description = "Get the details of a specific event by calendar and event ID.")]
237:     async fn event_get(
238:         &self,
239:         params: Parameters<EventGetParams>,
240:     ) -> Result<CallToolResult, rmcp::ErrorData> {
241:         let claims = CURRENT_CLAIMS
242:             .read()
243:             .await
244:             .clone()
245:             .ok_or_else(|| err("unauthenticated"))?;
246: 
247:         let (allowed_ids, scopes) = load_grant(&claims).await?;
248:         require_calendar(&allowed_ids, params.0.calendar_id)?;
249: 
250:         let has_details = scopes.iter().any(|s| s == "commoncal.event.read.details");
251:         let has_basic = scopes.iter().any(|s| s == "commoncal.event.read.basic");
252:         if !has_details && !has_basic {
253:             return Err(err(
254:                 "event_get requires commoncal.event.read.basic or commoncal.event.read.details",
255:             ));
256:         }
257: 
258:         let base = commoncal_base();
259:         let key = commoncal_bridge_key();
260:         let url = format!(
261:             "{}/internal/event?calendar_id={}&event_id={}",
262:             base, params.0.calendar_id, params.0.event_id
263:         );
264:         let resp = ECHO_HTTP
265:             .get(&url)
266:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", key))
267:             .send()
268:             .await
269:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("event_get transport: {e}")))?;
270:         if resp.status().as_u16() == 404 {
271:             return Err(err("event not found"));
272:         }
273:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
274:             return Err(err(format!("event_get failed: {}", resp.status())));
275:         }
276:         let body: serde_json::Value = resp
277:             .json()
278:             .await
279:             .map_err(|e| err(format!("event_get parse: {e}")))?;
280:         let event = body.get("event").cloned().unwrap_or(json!({}));
281: 
282:         let access = if has_details { "full" } else { "basic" };
283:         let output = if has_details {
284:             json!({ "event": event, "access": access })
285:         } else {
286:             let mut ev = event.clone();
287:             if let Some(obj) = ev.as_object_mut() {
288:                 obj.remove("description");
289:                 obj.remove("location");
290:             }
291:             json!({ "event": ev, "access": access })
292:         };
293: 
294:         Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(
295:             serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()),
296:         )]))
297:     }

342:         let events = body.get("events").cloned().unwrap_or(json!([]));
343: 
344:         let has_details = scopes.iter().any(|s| s == "commoncal.event.read.details");
345:         let access = if has_details { "full" } else { "basic" };

356:                             obj.remove("location");
357:                         }
358:                         ev
359:                     })
360:                     .collect()
361:             }
362:         } else {
363:             Vec::new()
364:         };
365: 
366:         let output = json!({ "events": output_events, "access": access });

368:             serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output).unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
369:         )]))

77:     privateKeyEncoding: { type: "pkcs8", format: "pem" },

85:     kid,

88:       n: jwk.n,

349:     }
350:     const client_id = params.get("client_id");
351:     if (client_id !== entry.client_id) {
352:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "client_id mismatch" } };
353:     }
354:     const redirect_uri = params.get("redirect_uri");
355:     if (redirect_uri !== entry.redirect_uri) {
356:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "redirect_uri mismatch" } };
357:     }
358:     const code_verifier = params.get("code_verifier");
359:     if (!code_verifier) {
360:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_request", error_description: "code_verifier required" } };
361:     }
362:     if (s256Challenge(code_verifier) !== entry.challenge) {
363:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "PKCE verifier mismatch" } };
364:     }
365: 
366:     entry.used = true;
367: 
368:     // The granted scopes are the intersection of requested and catalog
369:     // (slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs approvedResourceScopes).
370:     const requested = new Set(String(entry.scope).split(" ").filter(Boolean));
371:     const granted = SCOPE_CATALOG.filter((s) => requested.has(s));
372: 
373:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
374:     const jti = `mcp-acceptance-jti-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;
375:     const claims = {
376:       iss: this.issuer,
377:       sub: entry.sub,
378:       aud: this.resource,
379:       exp: now + 300,
380:       iat: now,
381:       jti,
382:       client_id: entry.client_id,
383:       scope: granted.join(" "),
384:       amr: ["pwd"],
385:     };
386:     const access_token = signJwt(claims, this.signingKey);
387:     this.tokens.set(jti, {
388:       client_id: entry.client_id,
389:       sub: entry.sub,
390:       scope: granted.join(" "),
391:       aud: this.resource,
392:       exp: claims.exp,
393:       iat: now,
394:     });
395: 
396:     return {
397:       status: 200,
398:       body: {
399:         access_token,
400:         token_type: "Bearer",
401:         expires_in: 300,
402:         refresh_token: `mcp-acceptance-refresh-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`,
403:         scope: granted.join(" "),
404:       },
405:     };
406:   }
407: 
408:   // -- JWKS -----------------------------------------------------------------
409: 
410:   /**
411:    * The JWKS document (public key only).
412:    */
413:   jwks() {
414:     return { keys: [this.signingKey.jwk] };
415:   }
416: 
417:   // -- Token validation (resource-server side) ------------------------------
418: 
419:   /**
420:    * Validate an access token the way the production MCP server must:
421:    * signature (via JWKS), exact iss, exact aud, exp, and the standard claims.
422:    * Returns { ok, claims?, error? }.
423:    */
424:   validateAccessToken(token) {
425:     if (typeof token !== "string" || token.split(".").length !== 3) {
426:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_token" };
427:     }
428:     const header = decodeJwtHeader(token);
429:     if (!header || header.alg !== "RS256") {
430:       return { ok: false, error: "unsupported_alg" };
431:     }
432:     const kid = header.kid;
433:     if (kid !== this.signingKey.kid) {
434:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_kid" };
435:     }
436:     if (!verifyJwtSignature(token, this.signingKey.jwk)) {
437:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_signature" };
438:     }
439:     const claims = decodeJwtPayload(token);
440:     if (!claims) {
441:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_payload" };
442:     }
443:     if (claims.iss !== this.issuer) {
444:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_issuer" };
445:     }
446:     const aud = Array.isArray(claims.aud) ? claims.aud : [claims.aud];
447:     if (!aud.includes(this.resource)) {
448:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_audience" };
449:     }
450:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
451:     if (typeof claims.exp !== "number" || claims.exp <= now) {
452:       return { ok: false, error: "token_expired" };
453:     }
454:     if (typeof claims.sub !== "string" || !/^\d+$/.test(claims.sub)) {
455:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_sub" };
456:     }
457:     if (typeof claims.client_id !== "string" || !this.clients.has(claims.client_id)) {
458:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_client" };
459:     }
460:     return { ok: true, claims };
461:   }
462: 
463:   // -- Token minting (verification-only) ------------------------------------
464: 
465:   /**
466:    * Mint a token with the given claims, signed with the provider's key.
467:    *
468:    * This is a verification-only helper used by the Phase 0.4 security harness
469:    * to drive the negative token cases (wrong issuer / audience / expiry /
470:    * client) with a VALID signature, so each claim check is exercised in
471:    * isolation (not masked by a signature failure). It is NOT part of the
472:    * production contract and is only reachable through the mock's `/_test/*`
473:    * hooks.
474:    *
475:    * @param {object} claims  The claims to embed in the token.
476:    * @returns {string} A signed JWT.
477:    */
478:   mintToken(claims) {
479:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
480:     const fullClaims = {
481:       iss: this.issuer,
482:       sub: "1",
483:       aud: this.resource,
484:       exp: now + 300,
485:       iat: now,
486:       jti: `mcp-acceptance-mint-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`,
487:       client_id: "mcp-acceptance-client-1",
488:       scope: SCOPE_CATALOG.join(" "),
489:       amr: ["pwd"],
490:       ...claims,
491:     };
492:     return signJwt(fullClaims, this.signingKey);
493:   }
494: 
495:   // -- Grants ---------------------------------------------------------------
496: 
497:   /**
498:    * Create an active grant for (sub, client_id) with the given allowed
499:    * calendar ids and scopes. Mirrors slice1-lab/src/bin/commoncal.rs
500:    * upsert_grant (replace semantics).
501:    */
502:   upsertGrant(sub, client_id, allowedCalendarIds, scopes) {
503:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
504:     this.grants.set(key, {
505:       sub,
506:       client_id,
507:       allowed_calendar_ids: allowedCalendarIds,
508:       scopes,
509:       revoked: false,
510:     });
511:   }
512: 
513:   /**
514:    * Revoke the active grant for (sub, client_id).
515:    */
516:   revokeGrant(sub, client_id) {
517:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
518:     const grant = this.grants.get(key);
519:     if (grant) grant.revoked = true;
520:   }
521: 
522:   /**
523:    * Delete the grant for (sub, client_id) entirely (simulates a missing grant).
524:    */
525:   deleteGrant(sub, client_id) {
526:     this.grants.delete(`${sub}:${client_id}`);
527:   }
528: 
529:   /**
530:    * Get the active grant for (sub, client_id), or null.
531:    */
532:   getActiveGrant(sub, client_id) {
533:     const grant = this.grants.get(`${sub}:${client_id}`);
534:     if (!grant || grant.revoked) return null;
535:     return grant;
536:   }
537: }

1: // event_search tool handler.
2: //
3: // Searches events in a calendar within a time range.
4: // Requires:
5: // - Valid OAuth token
6: // - McpGrant with allow_event_titles
7: // - Time range within max 31 days
8: // - Max 100 events returned
9: 
10: use axum::http::{Response, StatusCode};
11: use schemars::JsonSchema;
12: use serde::Deserialize;
13: 
14: use crate::error::ToolError;
15: use crate::internal_client::EventInfo;
16: use crate::mcp_grant::check_calendar_access;
17: use crate::output_schema::{
18:     ContentBlock, EventDescription, EventSearchOutput, EventSummary, ToolOutput,
19: };
20: use crate::tools::AuthorizedToolContext;
21: 
22: /// Maximum number of events to return.
23: const MAX_EVENTS: usize = 100;
24: 
25: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
26: pub struct EventSearchParams {
27:     /// The calendar to search in.
28:     pub calendar_id: i64,
29:     /// Start of the time range (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch seconds).
30:     pub from: String,
31:     /// End of the time range (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch seconds).
32:     pub to: String,
33:     /// Optional text query to filter events by title/description.
34:     pub query: Option<String>,
35: }
36: 
37: /// Handle the event_search tool call.
38: ///
39: /// Authorization pipeline:
40: /// 1. Gateway validates the OAuth token and resolves the authoritative grant.
41: /// 2. Check calendar access against the grant.
42: /// 3. Check the grant's tool permission.
43: /// 4. Validate time range (max 31 days).
44: /// 5. Call CommonCal core to search events.
45: /// 6. Limit to MAX_EVENTS.
46: /// 7. Return a structured response with access-level control.
47: pub async fn handle(
48:     context: &AuthorizedToolContext<'_>,
49:     params: EventSearchParams,
50: ) -> Result<Response<axum::body::Body>, ToolError> {
51:     let grant = context.grant;
52: 
53:     // Check calendar access against the authoritative grant.
54:     if !check_calendar_access(grant, params.calendar_id) {
55:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden("calendar not in grant".to_string()));
56:     }
57: 
58:     // Check tool permission.
59:     if !crate::mcp_grant::check_tool_permission(grant, "event_search") {
60:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden(
61:             "event_search requires event titles permission".to_string(),
62:         ));
63:     }
64: 
65:     // Step 4: Validate time range (reuse availability_find validation).
66:     let from_ts = crate::tools::availability_find::parse_utc_timestamp(&params.from)
67:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'from' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
68:     let to_ts = crate::tools::availability_find::parse_utc_timestamp(&params.to)
69:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'to' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
70: 
71:     if to_ts <= from_ts {
72:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(
73:             "'to' must be after 'from'".to_string(),
74:         ));
75:     }
76: 
77:     let range_secs = to_ts - from_ts;
78:     let max_secs = 31 * 24 * 3600;
79: 
80:     if range_secs > max_secs {
81:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(format!(
82:             "time range exceeds maximum of 31 days ({} seconds)",
83:             max_secs
84:         )));
85:     }
86: 
87:     // Search events via CommonCal core.
88:     let events = context
89:         .internal_client
90:         .search_events(params.calendar_id, &params.from, &params.to)
91:         .await
92:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::Internal(format!("event search failed: {}", e)))?;
93: 
94:     let has_more = events.len() > MAX_EVENTS;
95: 
96:     // Step 6: Limit to MAX_EVENTS.
97:     let limited: Vec<EventInfo> = events.into_iter().take(MAX_EVENTS).collect();
98:

100:     let access_level = if grant.allow_event_details {

102:     } else {

104:     };

124:                 }
125:             } else {
126:                 EventSummary {

128:                     calendar_id: e.calendar_id,

14: /// Open or create the configured SQLite file, apply embedded migrations, and
15: /// return a bounded pool.

17: /// Connection contract:
18: /// - `create_if_missing(true)`
19: /// - `foreign_keys(true)`
20: /// - `journal_mode(Wal)`
21: /// - `busy_timeout(5s)`
22: /// - `max_connections(5)`
23: pub async fn connect_and_migrate(database_path: &Path) -> Result<SqlitePool, sqlx::Error> {
24:     let options = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
25:         .filename(database_path)
26:         .create_if_missing(true)
27:         .foreign_keys(true)
28:         .journal_mode(SqliteJournalMode::Wal)
29:         .busy_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5));
30: 
31:     let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
32:         .max_connections(5)
33:         .connect_with(options)
34:         .await?;
35: 
36:     guard_duplicate_tables(&pool).await?;
37: 
38:     sqlx::migrate!("./migrations").run(&pool).await?;
39:     Ok(pool)

45: /// and `idempotency_key`. Those records have authoritative equivalents in
46: /// CommonCal core, but discarding data is an operator decision, not a
47: /// migration side effect: any row forces a human to reconcile first.
48: async fn guard_duplicate_tables(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
49:     for table in ["mcp_grant", "delete_intent", "idempotency_key"] {
50:         let exists = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>(
51:             "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = ?",

53:         .bind(table)
54:         .fetch_optional(pool)
55:         .await?

61:

66:         if rows > 0 {

433:     /// Create a unique mcp_grant for (user_id, oauth_client_id).
434:     /// Replaces any existing active grant (no union — replace semantics).
435:     /// Returns the grant ID.
436:     async fn upsert_grant(
437:         &self,
438:         user_id: i64,
439:         oauth_client_id: &str,
440:         allowed_calendar_ids: Vec<i64>,
441:         scopes: Vec<String>,
442:     ) -> String {
443:         let now = Self::now();
444:         let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
445: 
446:         // Revoke any existing active grant for this (user, client) pair.
447:         // This is "replace rather than union" semantics.
448:         for grant in st.grants.values_mut() {
449:             if grant.user_id == user_id
450:                 && grant.oauth_client_id == oauth_client_id
451:                 && grant.revoked_at.is_none()
452:             {
453:                 grant.revoked_at = Some(now);
454:             }
455:         }
456: 
457:         let grant_id = format!("grant_{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple());
458:         let grant = McpGrant {
459:             id: grant_id.clone(),
460:             user_id,
461:             oauth_client_id: oauth_client_id.to_string(),
462:             allowed_calendar_ids,
463:             scopes,
464:             created_at: now,
465:             revoked_at: None,
466:         };
467:         st.grants.insert(grant_id.clone(), grant);
468:         debug!(grant_id, user_id, oauth_client_id, "mcp_grant created");
469:         grant_id
470:     }

557:     /// Parse a UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch) to i64 seconds.
558:     fn parse_ts(s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
559:         if let Ok(ts) = s.parse::<i64>() {
560:             return Some(ts);
561:         }
562:         chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(s)
563:             .ok()
564:             .map(|dt| dt.timestamp())
565:     }
566: 
567:     /// Compute availability slots for a calendar in [from, to].
568:     /// A slot is "busy" if an event overlaps it, otherwise "free".
569:     /// Slots are 1-hour blocks aligned to the hour.
570:     async fn compute_availability(
571:         &self,
572:         calendar_id: i64,
573:         from: &str,
574:         to: &str,
575:     ) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
576:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
577:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
578:         let events: Vec<Event> = {
579:             let st = self.inner.read().await;
580:             st.events
581:                 .values()
582:                 .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
583:                 .cloned()
584:                 .collect()
585:         };
586: 
587:         let mut slots = Vec::new();
588:         let mut t = from_ts;
589:         while t < to_ts {
590:             let slot_end = (t + 3600).min(to_ts);
591:             let busy = events.iter().any(|e| {
592:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s < slot_end) && e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en > t)
593:             });
594:             slots.push(serde_json::json!({
595:                 "start": t,
596:                 "end": slot_end,
597:                 "status": if busy { "busy" } else { "free" },
598:             }));
599:             t = slot_end;
600:         }
601:         slots
602:     }
603: 
604:     /// Get a single event by (calendar_id, event_id).
605:     async fn get_event(&self, calendar_id: i64, event_id: i64) -> Option<Event> {
606:         let st = self.inner.read().await;
607:         st.events
608:             .get(&event_id)
609:             .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
610:             .cloned()
611:     }

613:     /// Search events in a calendar within [from, to], optionally filtered by query.
614:     async fn search_events(
615:         &self,
616:         calendar_id: i64,
617:         from: &str,
618:         to: &str,
619:         query: Option<&str>,
620:     ) -> Vec<Event> {
621:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
622:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
623:         let st = self.inner.read().await;
624:         let mut results: Vec<Event> = st
625:             .events
626:             .values()
627:             .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
628:             .filter(|e| {
629:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s >= from_ts && s <= to_ts)
630:                     || e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en >= from_ts && en <= to_ts)
631:             })
632:             .filter(|e| {
633:                 query.is_none_or(|q| {
634:                     let q_lower = q.to_lowercase();
635:                     e.title
636:                         .as_deref()
637:                         .is_some_and(|t| t.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
638:                         || e.description
639:                             .as_deref()
640:                             .is_some_and(|d| d.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
641:                 })
642:             })
643:             .cloned()
644:             .collect();
645:         drop(st);
646:         results.sort_by_key(|e| e.start_utc.unwrap_or(0));
647:         results
648:     }

689:     /// Create an event. Returns (event, was_idempotent_replay).
690:     #[expect(
691:         clippy::too_many_arguments,
692:         reason = "Lab helper mirrors the event request fields"
693:     )]
694:     async fn create_event(
695:         &self,
696:         calendar_id: i64,
697:         title: Option<String>,
698:         description: Option<String>,
699:         location: Option<String>,
700:         start_utc: Option<i64>,
701:         end_utc: Option<i64>,
702:         idempotency_key: Option<&str>,
703:     ) -> Result<(Event, bool), String> {
704:         let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
705:         if let Some(key) = idempotency_key
706:             && let Some(&existing_id) = st.idempotency_keys.get(key)
707:             && let Some(ev) = st.events.get(&existing_id)
708:         {
709:             return Ok((ev.clone(), true));
710:         }
711:         let id = st.next_event_id;
712:         st.next_event_id += 1;
713:         let event = Event {
714:             id,
715:             calendar_id,
716:             title,
717:             description,
718:             location,
719:             status: "confirmed".to_string(),
720:             event_kind: "default".to_string(),
721:             start_utc,
722:             end_utc,
723:             version: 1,
724:         };
725:         st.events.insert(id, event.clone());
726:         if let Some(key) = idempotency_key {
727:             st.idempotency_keys.insert(key.to_string(), id);
728:         }
729:         Ok((event, false))
730:     }

856:     /// Look up a handoff from the auth server's private API.
857:     async fn lookup_interaction(&self, handoff: &str) -> Result<InteractionView, String> {
858:         let url = format!(
859:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
860:             self.auth_private_base,
861:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
862:         );
863:         let resp = self
864:             .http
865:             .get(&url)
866:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
867:             .send()
868:             .await
869:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
870:         let status = resp.status();
871:         if !status.is_success() {
872:             let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
873:             tracing::error!(status = %status, body = %body, "lookup_interaction failed");
874:             return Err(format!("interaction lookup failed: {status} {body}"));
875:         }
876:         let body = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
877:         let view: InteractionView =
878:             serde_json::from_str(&body).map_err(|e| format!("parse interaction view: {e}"))?;
879:         Ok(view)
880:     }

882:     /// Decide a handoff (login/consent/deny) via the auth server's private API.
883:     /// `subject` is the authenticated CommonCal user id (the identity authority
884:     /// is CommonCal; the auth server binds the provider grant to this subject
885:     /// rather than a hardcoded value). Returns the resume URL.
886:     ///
887:     /// Honors the lab bridge-failure test hook: if armed, this call fails
888:     /// (simulating a bridge timeout) and the hook decrements, so a retry
889:     /// succeeds — proving grant-first / bridge-second idempotent retry.
890:     async fn decide_interaction(
891:         &self,
892:         handoff: &str,
893:         kind: &str,
894:         subject: Option<i64>,
895:     ) -> Result<String, String> {
896:         // Lab test hook: simulate a bridge failure on the next CONSENT decide
897:         // call(s). Only consent decisions are affected — the grant-first /
898:         // bridge-second ordering is a consent-path property, and login decisions
899:         // must not be disrupted (they precede the grant write).
900:         if kind == "consent" {
901:             let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
902:             if st.decide_fail_remaining > 0 {
903:                 st.decide_fail_remaining -= 1;
904:                 tracing::warn!("simulating bridge decide failure (test hook)");
905:                 return Err("simulated bridge timeout (test hook)".to_string());
906:             }
907:         }
908: 
909:         let url = format!(
910:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
911:             self.auth_private_base,
912:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
913:         );
914:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({ "kind": kind });
915:         if let Some(sub) = subject {
916:             body["subject"] = serde_json::json!(sub);
917:         }
918:         let resp = self
919:             .http
920:             .put(&url)
921:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
922:             .json(&body)
923:             .send()
924:             .await
925:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
926:         let status = resp.status();
927:         if !status.is_success() {
928:             let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
929:             tracing::error!(status = %status, text = %text, "decide_interaction failed");
930:             return Err(format!("interaction decide failed: {status} {text}"));
931:         }
932:         let result: serde_json::Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
933:         result
934:             .get("resumeUrl")
935:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
936:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
937:             .ok_or_else(|| "decide response missing resumeUrl".to_string())
938:     }
939: }

954: /// GET /consent?handoff=...
955: ///
956: /// If the interaction prompt is "login" and the user has a session, decide
957: /// login immediately (redirect to resume URL). If the prompt is "consent",
958: /// render the consent page. If no session, redirect to /login.
959: async fn consent_page(
960:     State(state): State<AppState>,
961:     Query(q): Query<ConsentQuery>,
962:     headers: HeaderMap,
963: ) -> Response {
964:     let handoff = match &q.handoff {
965:         Some(h) if !h.is_empty() => h.clone(),
966:         _ => {
967:             return (
968:                 StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
969:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": "missing_handoff"})),
970:             )
971:                 .into_response();
972:         }
973:     };
974: 
975:     // Look up the interaction from the auth server.
976:     let view = match state.lookup_interaction(&handoff).await {
977:         Ok(v) => v,
978:         Err(e) => {
979:             return (
980:                 StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
981:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
982:             )
983:                 .into_response();
984:         }
985:     };
986: 
987:     // Check if the user has a session.
988:     let session_token = extract_session_cookie(&headers);
989:     let user_id = match &session_token {
990:         Some(t) => state.get_session(t).await,
991:         None => None,
992:     };
993: 
994:     // If no session, redirect to login with a continue param.
995:     let continue_url = format!("/consent?handoff={}", urlencoding::encode(&handoff));
996:     let (session_token, user_id) = match (&session_token, user_id) {
997:         (Some(t), Some(uid)) => (t.clone(), uid),
998:         _ => {
999:             let location = format!("/login?continue={}", urlencoding::encode(&continue_url));
1000:             return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, location)]).into_response();
1001:         }
1002:     };
1003: 
1004:     // If the prompt is "login", decide login immediately (user is authenticated).
1005:     if view.prompt == "login" {
1006:         match state
1007:             .decide_interaction(&handoff, "login", Some(user_id))
1008:             .await
1009:         {
1010:             Ok(resume_url) => {
1011:                 return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, resume_url)]).into_response();
1012:             }
1013:             Err(e) => {
1014:                 return (
1015:                     StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
1016:                     Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
1017:                 )
1018:                     .into_response();
1019:             }
1020:         }
1021:     }

1023:     // If the prompt is "consent", render the consent page.

1027:             .requested_scopes
1028:             .iter()
1029:             .map(|s| format!("<li>{}</li>", escape_html(s)))
1030:             .collect();
1031:         let html = format!(
1032:             r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
1033: <html lang="en">
1034: <head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>CommonCal — Authorize</title>
1035: <style>body{{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;max-width:480px;margin:2rem auto;padding:0 1rem}}
1036: .card{{border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;padding:1.5rem;margin-top:1rem}}
1037: button{{padding:.5rem 1rem;margin-right:.5rem;cursor:pointer;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid #ccc}}
1038: .approve{{background:#22c55e;color:#fff;border-color:#16a34a}}
1039: .deny{{background:#fff;color:#dc2626;border-color:#dc2626}}
1040: ul{{padding-left:1.2rem}}</style></head>
1041: <body>
1042: <h1>Authorize access</h1>
1043: <div class="card">
1044: <p><strong>{}</strong> is requesting access to your CommonCal account.</p>

1048: <input type="hidden" name="handoff" value="{}">

1050: <button type="submit" name="decision" value="approve" class="approve">Approve</button>
1051: <button type="submit" name="decision" value="deny" class="deny">Deny</button>
1052: </form>
1053: </div>
1054: </body></html>"#,
1055:             escape_html(&view.client_name),
1056:             scopes_html.join(""),
1057:             escape_html(&handoff),
1058:             escape_html(&csrf_token),

1060:         return (
1061:             StatusCode::OK,

1064:         )

1233: async fn consent_decision(
1234:     State(state): State<AppState>,
1235:     headers: HeaderMap,
1236:     body: axum::body::Bytes,
1237: ) -> Response {
1238:     let params = parse_form(&body);
1239:     let handoff = match params.get("handoff").cloned() {
1240:         Some(h) => h,
1241:         None => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "missing handoff").into_response(),
1242:     };
1243:     let csrf = match params.get("csrf").cloned() {
1244:         Some(c) => c,
1245:         None => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "missing csrf").into_response(),
1246:     };
1247:     let decision = match params.get("decision").cloned() {
1248:         Some(d) if d == "approve" || d == "deny" => d,
1249:         _ => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "invalid decision").into_response(),
1250:     };
1251: 
1252:     // Validate session.
1253:     let session_token = match extract_session_cookie(&headers) {
1254:         Some(t) => t,
1255:         None => return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "no session").into_response(),
1256:     };
1257:     let user_id = match state.get_session(&session_token).await {
1258:         Some(id) => id,
1259:         None => return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "invalid session").into_response(),
1260:     };

299:  * Exchange an authorization code for a token (Authorization Code + S256 PKCE).

310:   const params = new URLSearchParams({
311:     grant_type: "authorization_code",
312:     code,
313:     redirect_uri: redirect,

327:  *
328:  * @param {object} cfg  Harness configuration.
329:  * @param {string} issuer  The issuer base URL.

335:     dcr: null,
336:     authorize: null,
337:     token: null,
338:   };

340:   // 1. DCR.
341:   const dcrResp = await dcrRegister(cfg, issuer, redirect);
342:   record.dcr = dcrResp;

348:   // 2. Authorization Code + S256 PKCE.
349:   const verifier = generateVerifier();

358:   const tokenResp = await tokenExchange(cfg, issuer, authResult.code, clientId, redirect, verifier);
359:   record.token = tokenResp;
360:   const accessToken = tokenResp.bodyJson && tokenResp.bodyJson.access_token;

362:   return { accessToken, clientId, record };

425:   function sort(value) {
426:     if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sort);
427:     if (isPlainObject(value)) {
428:       const out = {};
429:       for (const key of Object.keys(value).sort()) {
430:         out[key] = sort(value[key]);
431:       }
432:       return out;
433:     }
434:     return value;
435:   }
436:   return JSON.stringify(sort(value), null, 2);
437: }

1: // calendar_list tool handler.
2: //
3: // Returns the user's calendars filtered by McpGrant permissions.
4: // Requires:
5: // - Valid OAuth token
6: // - McpGrant with calendar metadata read permission
7: // - Calendar IDs in grant's allowed_calendar_ids
8:

14: use crate::mcp_grant::check_calendar_access;

16: use crate::tools::AuthorizedToolContext;
17: 
18: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
19: pub struct CalendarListParams {
20:     /// Whether to include access-level details in the response.
21:     #[serde(default)]
22:     pub include_access: bool,
23: }
24: 
25: /// Handle the calendar_list tool call.
26: ///
27: /// Authorization pipeline:
28: /// 1. Auth middleware validates the OAuth token and publishes the identity.
29: /// 2. Service layer resolves the authoritative grant.
30: /// 3. Check the grant's calendar-list permission.
31: /// 4. Call CommonCal core to list calendars.
32: /// 5. Filter by the grant's allowed_calendar_ids.
33: /// 6. Return the structured response.
34: pub async fn handle(
35:     context: &AuthorizedToolContext<'_>,
36:     _params: CalendarListParams,
37: ) -> Result<Response<axum::body::Body>, ToolError> {
38:     let grant = context.grant;
39: 
40:     // Check tool permission against the authoritative grant.
41:     //
42:     // calendar_list is a calendar-metadata read; it is gated by the
43:     // availability/metadata capability, NOT by the availability_find tool
44:     // capability. (Previously this checked the wrong capability.)
45:     if !crate::mcp_grant::check_tool_permission(grant, "calendar_list") {
46:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden(
47:             "calendar_list requires calendar metadata read permission".to_string(),
48:         ));
49:     }
50: 
51:     // Fetch calendars from CommonCal core.
52:     let calendars = context
53:         .internal_client
54:         .list_calendars(context.token.user_id)
55:         .await
56:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::Internal(format!("calendar fetch failed: {}", e)))?;
57: 
58:     // Filter by the grant's allowed calendars.
59:     let filtered: Vec<CalendarSummary> = calendars
60:         .into_iter()
61:         .filter(|c| check_calendar_access(grant, c.id))
62:         .map(|c| CalendarSummary {
63:             id: c.id,
64:             name: c.name,
65:             color: String::new(),
66:             access: c.access,
67:         })
68:         .collect();
69: 
70:     // Build structured response.
71:     let output = ToolOutput {
72:         content: vec![ContentBlock::Text {
73:             text: serde_json::to_string_pretty(&CalendarListOutput {
74:                 calendars: filtered,
75:             })
76:             .unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
77:         }],
78:     };
79: 
80:     let body = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output)
81:         .unwrap_or_else(|_| r#"{"content":[{"text":"[]"}]}"#.to_string());
82: 
83:     Ok(Response::builder()
84:         .status(StatusCode::OK)
85:         .header("content-type", "application/json")
86:         .body(axum::body::Body::from(body))
87:         .unwrap())
88: }

1: // event_search tool handler.
2: //
3: // Searches events in a calendar within a time range.
4: // Requires:
5: // - Valid OAuth token
6: // - McpGrant with allow_event_titles
7: // - Time range within max 31 days
8: // - Max 100 events returned
9: 
10: use axum::http::{Response, StatusCode};
11: use schemars::JsonSchema;
12: use serde::Deserialize;
13: 
14: use crate::error::ToolError;
15: use crate::internal_client::EventInfo;
16: use crate::mcp_grant::check_calendar_access;
17: use crate::output_schema::{
18:     ContentBlock, EventDescription, EventSearchOutput, EventSummary, ToolOutput,
19: };
20: use crate::tools::AuthorizedToolContext;
21: 
22: /// Maximum number of events to return.
23: const MAX_EVENTS: usize = 100;
24: 
25: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
26: pub struct EventSearchParams {
27:     /// The calendar to search in.
28:     pub calendar_id: i64,
29:     /// Start of the time range (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch seconds).
30:     pub from: String,
31:     /// End of the time range (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch seconds).
32:     pub to: String,
33:     /// Optional text query to filter events by title/description.
34:     pub query: Option<String>,
35: }
36: 
37: /// Handle the event_search tool call.
38: ///
39: /// Authorization pipeline:
40: /// 1. Gateway validates the OAuth token and resolves the authoritative grant.
41: /// 2. Check calendar access against the grant.
42: /// 3. Check the grant's tool permission.
43: /// 4. Validate time range (max 31 days).
44: /// 5. Call CommonCal core to search events.
45: /// 6. Limit to MAX_EVENTS.
46: /// 7. Return a structured response with access-level control.
47: pub async fn handle(
48:     context: &AuthorizedToolContext<'_>,
49:     params: EventSearchParams,
50: ) -> Result<Response<axum::body::Body>, ToolError> {
51:     let grant = context.grant;
52: 
53:     // Check calendar access against the authoritative grant.
54:     if !check_calendar_access(grant, params.calendar_id) {
55:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden("calendar not in grant".to_string()));
56:     }
57: 
58:     // Check tool permission.
59:     if !crate::mcp_grant::check_tool_permission(grant, "event_search") {
60:         return Err(ToolError::Forbidden(
61:             "event_search requires event titles permission".to_string(),
62:         ));
63:     }
64: 
65:     // Step 4: Validate time range (reuse availability_find validation).
66:     let from_ts = crate::tools::availability_find::parse_utc_timestamp(&params.from)
67:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'from' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
68:     let to_ts = crate::tools::availability_find::parse_utc_timestamp(&params.to)
69:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::BadRequest(format!("invalid 'to' timestamp: {}", e)))?;
70: 
71:     if to_ts <= from_ts {
72:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(
73:             "'to' must be after 'from'".to_string(),
74:         ));
75:     }
76: 
77:     let range_secs = to_ts - from_ts;
78:     let max_secs = 31 * 24 * 3600;
79: 
80:     if range_secs > max_secs {
81:         return Err(ToolError::BadRequest(format!(
82:             "time range exceeds maximum of 31 days ({} seconds)",
83:             max_secs
84:         )));
85:     }
86: 
87:     // Search events via CommonCal core.
88:     let events = context
89:         .internal_client
90:         .search_events(params.calendar_id, &params.from, &params.to)
91:         .await
92:         .map_err(|e| ToolError::Internal(format!("event search failed: {}", e)))?;
93: 
94:     let has_more = events.len() > MAX_EVENTS;
95: 
96:     // Step 6: Limit to MAX_EVENTS.
97:     let limited: Vec<EventInfo> = events.into_iter().take(MAX_EVENTS).collect();
98: 
99:     // Step 7: Build structured response.
100:     let access_level = if grant.allow_event_details {
101:         "full"
102:     } else {
103:         "basic"
104:     };
105: 
106:     let event_summaries: Vec<EventSummary> = limited
107:         .iter()
108:         .map(|e| {
109:             if access_level == "full" {
110:                 EventSummary {
111:                     id: e.id,
112:                     calendar_id: e.calendar_id,
113:                     title: e.title.clone(),
114:                     description: e.description.as_ref().map(|d| EventDescription {
115:                         value: d.clone(),
116:                         trust: "user_supplied_untrusted",
117:                     }),
118:                     location: e.location.clone(),
119:                     status: e.status.clone(),
120:                     event_kind: e.event_kind.clone(),
121:                     start_utc: e.start_utc.map(|t| t.to_string()),
122:                     end_utc: e.end_utc.map(|t| t.to_string()),
123:                     version: e.version.unwrap_or(0),
124:                 }
125:             } else {
126:                 EventSummary {
127:                     id: e.id,
128:                     calendar_id: e.calendar_id,
129:                     title: e.title.clone(),
130:                     description: None,
131:                     location: None,
132:                     status: e.status.clone(),
133:                     event_kind: e.event_kind.clone(),
134:                     start_utc: e.start_utc.map(|t| t.to_string()),
135:                     end_utc: e.end_utc.map(|t| t.to_string()),
136:                     version: e.version.unwrap_or(0),
137:                 }
138:             }
139:         })
140:         .collect();
141: 
142:     let output = EventSearchOutput {
143:         events: event_summaries,
144:         next_page: if has_more {
145:             Some("page_token_placeholder".to_string())
146:         } else {
147:             None
148:         },
149:     };
150: 
151:     let tool_output = ToolOutput {
152:         content: vec![ContentBlock::Text {
153:             text: serde_json::to_string_pretty(&output).unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".to_string()),
154:         }],
155:     };
156: 
157:     let body = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&tool_output)
158:         .unwrap_or_else(|_| r#"{"content":[{"text":"[]"}]}"#.to_string());
159: 
160:     Ok(Response::builder()
161:         .status(StatusCode::OK)
162:         .header("content-type", "application/json")
163:         .body(axum::body::Body::from(body))
164:         .unwrap())
165: }

170:

172:     fn event_search_params_deserializes_with_query() {
